name: Sirona

attributes.attribute: depicted with a serpent and an egg
Celtic god with whom Sirona was often linked

sources: Green, Miranda. Symbol and Image in Celtic Religious Art. London: Routledge, 1989, 43.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Sirona is a Continental Celtic goddess. Her name has been read as the word for star. It appears also as Dirona, and possibly as Tsirona. Many inscriptions in France and in other Celtic lands call on her as a healing goddess. She was often connected with the Celtic Apollo, yet she also stood alone. Her images show a serpent and an egg, which are signs of rebirth and of fertility. A shrine at Hochscheid was raised for her cult. Koch links her with Apollo Grunnus, and he sets her beside the mother-goddesses who are called the Matronae. Her name may tie to the female calf, Damona. The many inscriptions and statues show a goddess who kept her own worship even as she stood beside the risen god. She held the healing of the body and the promise of the year., and the stones that name her keep that power.
